findings.summary: traced() still reads any non-zero git exit (dubious ownership, corrupt store, etc.) as 'no marker', so git failing without a timeout still makes the repo untraced and lets the edit through. Also raised by the spec subagent in the same round.
findings.reason: Confirmed from the diff: git() returns null for non-zero status and traced() treats null as 'no'; cat-file -e exits 128 for both missing and real failures, so acceptance criterion 1 ('when git cannot say... refuse') is only partially met. Agent fixed with --batch-check.

findings.summary: git() does not treat a signal-killed git (status null, no r.error) as an error; returns null so traced() fails open.
findings.reason: spawnSync on external SIGKILL yields status null with no error; git() returns null and traced() says untraced. A real, if narrow, fail-open gap against the issue's criterion; agent fixed it.

findings.summary: When defaultBranch() returns null (no origin/HEAD, no main/master), traced() checks only HEAD, so a branch committing the marker's deletion opts itself out.
findings.reason: Pre-existing limitation of the default-branch heuristic; git did answer, so it is outside the issue's scope. Agent reasonably deferred as a follow-up.

findings.summary: archiveBlock now draws on the shared 20s deadline before the trace runs; chained history commands can exhaust it so traceReason → commandVerdict → tracedRoot → traced() throws and an untraced repository gets 'trace could not be checked'. Archive OutOfTime also hides the trace verdict/TRACE_BYPASS hint.
findings.reason: A real consequence of the PR: with traced() now throwing, any deadline exhaustion yields a deny even in untraced repos. However it attributes the refusal to the archive draining the deadline and never identifies the actual defect (where() called eagerly by commitVerdict/prVerdict refusing read-only git/gh commands whenever git is slow), so it does not meet the same-defect standard for the in-diff bug.

findings.summary: historyTouches returns true (deny as 'would print changes in the archive') when git is stopped at its own 5s cap, or by a signal / ENOBUFS, rather than saying git could not answer.
findings.reason: Correct observation but the behaviour fails closed and predates the PR ('when git cannot say, assume the worst'); only the deny wording is imprecise. Repeated in round 2 (signal/ENOBUFS variant). Agent changed it anyway.

findings.summary: archiveBlock is called outside any try; any error it throws other than OutOfTime is rethrown to hook.mjs's top-level fail-open catch, which skips the trace gate as well, allowing the edit/commit/PR.
findings.reason: Names exactly the known pre-existing bug: archive-block errors other than running out of time reach the 'Fail open' catch at hook.mjs:82. Agent declined to fix, calling the outer catch deliberate.

findings.summary: Other tracedRoot callers (status band, stopNudge, issueContext, readRecord) now throw in untraced repos when git is missing/slow: status exits 1, other hooks print errors to stderr. Also raised by the spec subagent.
findings.reason: A real behaviour change in non-gate paths but not a confirmed defect; hook.mjs already treats a status failure as 'not untraced' and the agent judged it intended. Not the known in-diff bug (which is about read-only git/gh commands being refused).

findings.summary: Deadline handling is duplicated: mutable module-level timeLeft and an OutOfTime class in archive.mjs re-implement trace.mjs's deadline; later rounds restate it as 'one shared git runner would fix both'.
findings.reason: Refactoring/style preference with no failure named; repeated in rounds 2 and 3 as 'root-cause duplication' / 'altitude'. Agent declined with a reasonable rationale.

findings.summary: traced() spawns up to three sequential cat-file -e processes per repository; a single cat-file --batch-check would answer all revisions at once and use less of the shared deadline.
findings.reason: Performance suggestion with only a speculative 'more likely to time out' consequence; no concrete failure. Agent adopted batch-check as part of the non-zero-exit fix.

findings.summary: The timeout test's env { PATH: ... } replaces the PATH the hook() helper builds, dropping the fake gh so the real gh could be used if evaluation order changes.
findings.reason: Test hygiene; the test passes today and the concern is a hypothetical ordering change. Agent fixed it.

findings.summary: Standards subagent: ADR 0006 says the trace applies only in opted-in repositories and every deny names a pipeline step, but the PR now gates unmarked repos when git cannot answer and the could-not-be-checked deny names the bypass. Suggests amending the ADR.
findings.location: docs/adr/0006 vs test/trace.test.mjs rewritten no-git test
findings.reason: Documentation tension / design judgement, not a code defect; the issue's own criterion 1 requires refusing when git cannot say. Agent escalated to the human.

findings.summary: Standards subagent smells: left() is a mysterious name for something called for its throw; timeLeft optional on World / default deadline is speculative generality; archive.test.mjs importing worldFor and asserting on world.git.message is feature envy.
findings.location: plugins/trace/scripts/lib/archive.mjs left(), trace.mjs World typedef, test/archive.test.mjs
findings.reason: Pure style preferences with no failure named. Agent renamed left() to timeLeftOrStop().

findings.summary: Spec subagent: the archive deadline sharing, OutOfTime class, new Bash denial message and hook.mjs wiring are scope creep beyond the issue, which is only about traced().
findings.reason: Scope judgement, not a defect; the agent gave a defensible rationale (archive 5s checks on top of the 20s deadline could exceed the 30s hook timeout) and kept it.

findings.summary: Spec subagent: the timeout tests cover only the edit gate; commit and PR are covered only by the no-git test, not a timeout test.
findings.reason: Acceptance criterion 3 ('a test covers the timeout case') is met; extending coverage is nice-to-have. Agent extended the tests.

findings.summary: Spec subagent / round 2: on a machine with no runnable git, or a repository git cannot read (dubious ownership, dangling .git worktree pointer), every repository is now gated, marker or not; a broken nested .git blocks everything beneath it.
findings.reason: Consequence of implementing the issue's criterion 1 literally ('when git cannot say... refuse'); a design tradeoff rather than a confirmed defect, and not the known in-diff bug (which concerns read-only commands via eager where()). Repeated in round 2 finding 4.

findings.summary: cat-file --batch-check also prints 'missing' when an object is unreadable (corrupt pack, partial clone), so traced() still treats 'git could not say' as untraced.
findings.reason: Speculative edge case I cannot confirm; git generally fails loudly on corrupt stores. Agent reasonably deferred as a follow-up.

findings.summary: Any batch-check line that is not '... missing' counts as 'has the marker', including 'ambiguous' answers and an empty stdout (''.split('\n') → ['']), so an untraced repo could become traced.
findings.reason: Concrete parsing flaw in the agent's round-1 fix: an empty or unexpected answer is read as 'present', wrongly gating an untraced repository. Agent confirmed by fixing and testing it.

findings.summary: The shared git() helper now throws on any signal-terminated git, changing every caller (origin, ghBase, committed, pushed, branch, ...) that used to get null and fall back.
findings.reason: Observation about blast radius of the round-1 fix; consistent with how timeouts already threw for every call. No concrete defect named. Agent declined.

findings.summary: A git stopped at its own 5s per-call cap is reported as OutOfTime with the hint 'Run fewer of them at once', which does not apply when only one command ran.
findings.reason: Deny-message wording nit; the deny itself is correct (fail closed).

findings.summary: The archive test's fake git sleeps on any argv containing ' log ', including the trace's git log calls (message, committed); passes only due to evaluation order and costs 5s per run.
findings.reason: Test fragility/hygiene with no present failure. Agent narrowed the shim.

findings.summary: gitThat() and the archive test leave mkdtemp git-* directories in tmpdir, and the timeout test pays 3s three times.
findings.reason: Test housekeeping; the existing hook() helper does the same. Agent declined.

findings.summary: traced() asks git about short names origin/<def> and <def>; a tag named 'main' or a local branch named 'origin/main' pointing at a pre-marker commit shadows the real refs, git answers 'missing', and the repo is treated as untraced. Use refs/remotes/origin/<def> and refs/heads/<def>.
findings.reason: Confirmed: the diff uses short rev names; git's rev resolution prefers refs/tags/<name> over refs/heads/<name>, so a decoy tag defeats the default-branch check. Pre-existing but a real bypass; agent reproduced it in a test and fixed it.

findings.summary: Any r.error now raises NoAnswer, including ENOENT/EACCES/ENOBUFS, and the archive deny message ('Run fewer of them at once' / 'git gave no answer') does not say the cause, unlike the trace's deny which names the signal.
findings.reason: Deny-message clarity; the command is still refused. Agent made NoAnswer carry the cause.

findings.summary: The fake git now intercepts every call with --name-only, including the trace's ls-tree in headDocs, so the test could pass or fail via a different code path if evaluation order changes.
findings.reason: Hypothetical test fragility; no present failure.

findings.summary: The archive test re-implements the fake-git PATH shim already in trace.test.mjs's gitThat(); move it to a shared helper.
findings.reason: Test code reuse preference. Agent declined.

findings.summary: answers.every(missing) is evaluated twice and object lines are matched with a hand-written regex; use --batch-check=%(objecttype) and classify each line once.
findings.reason: Simplification suggestion with no failure named. Agent adopted it.

fixed.reason: The diff does not touch commitVerdict/prVerdict or the eager where() call that precedes command classification. It only changes how traced()/historyTouches() decide and what errors they throw (now also throwing on signals and unreadable repos), so a slow or missing git still causes where() to throw before the hook learns the command is a read-only `git status` or `gh issue view`, and those commands are still refused in untraced repos. No test covers a read-only command under a slow git either; the new tests only assert Edit/commit/PR are denied.
